study_info.title: Effect of obstructive sleep apnoea and its treatment with continuous positive airway pressure on the prevalence of cardiovascular events in patients with acute coronary syndrome (ISAACC study): a randomised controlled trial
study_info.authors: Manuel Sánchez-de-la-Torre, Alicia Sánchez-de-la-Torre, Sandra Bertran, Jorge Abad, Joaquín Duran-Cantolla, Valentín Cabriada, Olga Mediano, María José Masdeu, Mari Luz Alonso, Juan Fernando Masa, Antonia Barceló, Mónica de la Peña, Mercè Mayos, Ramón Coloma, Josep M Montserrat, Eusebi Chiner, Salvador Perelló, Gemma Rubinós, Olga Mínguez, Lydia Pascual, Anunciación Cortijo, Dolores Martínez, Albina Aldomà, Mireia Dalmases, R Doug McEvoy, Ferran Barbé, on behalf of the Spanish Sleep Network
study_info.study_design: Multicentre, open-label, parallel-group, randomised controlled trial. Simple randomisation was done by a computerised system available 24 h a day via a fully secure, password-protected study website using the rand() function in PHP 7.3.
study_info.inclusion_criteria: Patients aged 18 years and older, admitted to hospital for documented symptoms of ACS, with a hospital stay of 24–72 h at the time of sleep study, and an Epworth Sleepiness Scale (EES) score of 10 or less (non-sleepy).
study_info.exclusion_criteria: Previous treatment with CPAP for OSA; psychophysical inability to complete questionnaires; presence of any previously diagnosed sleep disorder; more than 50% central apnoeas or the presence of Cheyne–Stokes respiration; daytime sleepiness (ESS >10); chronic diseases; a medical history that could interfere with the study objectives or compromise conclusions; any medical factor, social or geographical, that might jeopardise patient compliance; any processes that reduce life expectancy to less than 1 year; and cardiogenic shock.
study_info.source_of_recruitment: Patients admitted to hospital for acute coronary syndrome (ACS)
study_info.number_of_participants_randomized: 1264 patients with OSA were randomly assigned to the CPAP group (n=633) or the UC group (n=631).
study_info.number_of_participants_analyzed: 2551 patients were recruited. 1264 patients with OSA were randomized. 1287 patients did not have OSA, of whom 603 were randomly assigned to the reference group.

minimal_units.adherence_to_intervention: Mean time of adherence to CPAP treatment was 2.78 h/night (SD 2·73).
